sentences.text: JUDGMENT Not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation, appellant who is claimant No.2 before the Tribunal has filed this appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) seeking enhancement of compensation for the death of her son Iranna in a motor vehicles accident dated 26.06.2014.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. Subsequent to passing of the award, petitioner No.1 died and therefore he is not arraigned as appellant in this appeal.
4. It is the case of the petitioners that on 26.06.2014 their son Iranna was travelling in bullock cart to go to his agricultural land.
At about 6:45 a.m. when he was near toll naka, accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of tanker bearing Reg.No.MH-12-HD-3524.
Due to severe injuries, he died on the spot.
Petitioners have lost their bread earner.
As owner and insurer, respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
5. Respondent No.1 has remained ex parte.

6. Respondent No.2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the age,
occupation, income of the deceased and that accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

As on the date of accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence and as such respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
7.
Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.

8. On behalf of petitioners, petitioner No.2 is examined as PW.1 and one witness as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P1 to 10.
9.
On behalf of respondent No.2, no oral or documentary evidence is led.

10. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal partly allowed the claim petition and granted compensation in a sum of Rs.8,25,000/- with interest at 9% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.

sentences.text:
The details of the compensation granted by the Tribunal are as below:
 Sl.No.

Compensation head Amount  awarded  1. Loss of dependency Rs.7,65,000/-
 2. Loss of love and affection Rs.30,000/-
 3. Loss of estate Rs.10,000/-
 4. Transportation of dead body Rs.10,000/-
5 . Funeral expenses Rs.10,000/-
Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.

13. During the course of arguments, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that having regard to the age, occupation of the deceased the compensation granted is on the lower side and it requires reconsideration.
14. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and prays to dismiss the appeal.

15. Heard arguments and perused the records.
16.

Having regard to the specific grounds urged in the appeal, it is necessary to examine whether the compensation granted by the Tribunal is just and reasonable or it calls for interference by this Court under the following various heads.
17. Loss of dependency: Based on the medical records, the Tribunal has rightly considered the age of deceased at 28 years and therefore '17' as the appropriate multiplier.
Having regard to the fact that accident is of the year 2014, the Tribunal has correctly assessed the notional income of the deceased as Rs.7,500/-.

However, it has not granted any amount towards loss of future prospects as required under Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1 (Magma Insurance Company case).

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1 (Magma Insurance Company case)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since petitioner was aged less than 40 years, 40% of income is required to be added towards loss of future prospects.
Since the deceased was bachelor, 50% is required to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
With these components, the loss of dependency is Rs.10,500/- x 12 x 17 x 50% =Rs.10,71,000/- as against Rs.7,65,000/- granted by the Tribunal.
18. Loss of consortium:
The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.30,000/- under the head loss of love and affection.

As per National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others2 (Pranay Sethi's case) and Magma Insurance Company case, as parents, petitioners are entitled for compensation at Rs.40,000/- each.

Rs.30,000/- granted under the head loss of love and affection is disallowed.

sentences.text: Loss to estate and funeral expenses:
The Tribunal has granted Rs.10,000/- each under the head loss of estate and transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.

When substantial compensation is granted under the head loss of dependency, as per Pranay Sethi's case and Magma Insurance Company case, under the conventional head loss to estate and funeral expenses (which includes transportation of dead body) Rs.15,000/- each is required to be granted under these two heads.
Accordingly, the same is granted.
Consequently, Rs.10,000/- each granted under the head loss of estate, transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is disallowed.

20. Thus, in all petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.11,81,000/- as against Rs.8,25,000/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:
Sl. Heads Amount awarded Amount awarded No. by the Tribunal by this Court 1. Loss of Rs.7,65,000/- Rs.10,71,000/-
dependency 2. Loss of consortium Rs.30,000/- Rs.80,000/-
(loss of love and affection)
3. Loss to estate Rs.10,000/- Rs.15,000/-
4.

Funeral expenses Rs.10,000/- Rs.15,000/-
Rs.10,000/-
(transportation of dead body) Total Rs.8,25,000/- Rs.11,81,000/-
21.

To this extent the impugned judgment and award is required to be modified and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) Appellant/petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.11,81,000/-
together with interest at 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation as against Rs.8,25,000/-
granted by the Tribunal.

(iii) Respondent No.2 is directed to pay the compensation together with accrued interest at 6%
(minus the amount already paid/deposited) on the enhanced compensation within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
